mainTopic: Where a thrown גט takes effect (roofs, courtyards, baskets), using a גט ישן, and the penalties for a wrongly dated גט
overview: This amud opens by finishing a list of points about roofs. On שבת, שמואל says each roof is its own separate area. For a גט, though, a neighboring roof of the husband still works, because a husband does not mind her using it. אביי then rules on a case where her courtyard sits inside his, and his walls are taller than hers. In that case a thrown גט counts as hers once it drops below his walls. Baskets work differently: the גט must actually land in her basket, and this works only if his outer basket has no bottom. A new משנה follows. בית שמאי and בית הלל argue about a גט ישן, and the גמרא explains that the argument is about a גזרה that people might think her divorce came before her son. Another משנה lists improper ways to date or place a גט. If she remarried using such a גט, she must leave both husbands, loses her money rights, and faces other penalties as well.

steps.title: שמואל's rule: each roof is a separate area
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רב יהודה in the name of שמואל. A person may not collect rainwater from his neighbor's roof, because roofs are separate areas just like the homes below them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the rule that רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: a person should not stand on this roof and catch rainwater from his friend's roof. Just as the homes are separate below, the homes are also separate above.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a rule of שמואל about roofs being separate areas. This is setting up the next step, which will limit where the rule applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's point is that a roof belongs to the home under it. So two roofs are two separate areas, even though nobody lives on a roof. On its own, this could suggest that a גט landing on a neighboring roof is in a totally different place.

keyTerms.meaning: Above, here meaning up on the roofs

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: And that which Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel:
A person should not stand on this roof
and catch rainwater
from the roof of his fellow,
phrases.notes: This is a שבת rule: without an עירוב joining the homes, you can't bring things from one person's area into another's.

phrases.english: for just as the dwellings are separate below,
so too the dwellings are separate above –

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of roof-related points from earlier on the daf by quoting שמואל's rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On שבת, each roof is a separate area, so you may not take rainwater from a neighbor's roof (without an עירוב).

steps.title: That rule is only for שבת, not for a גט
steps.stepSummary: שמואל's rule applies only to שבת. For a גט, the question is whether the husband would mind. People do not mind to that extent, so a neighboring roof of his still works.
steps.simpleTranslation: That rule is only about שבת. But for a גט, the issue is whether the husband minds, and people are not that particular.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא limits שמואל's rule to שבת and says it does not decide גט cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גט normally has to land in a place the husband has let her use. Usually she gets only that one place, because a husband is particular about what he lends. But a husband would not mind her using his roof right next to the one he lent her. So a גט landing there still divorces her, even though on שבת the two roofs count as separate areas.

keyTerms.meaning: These words apply (only to this case)

steps.whatToRemember: The rules about separate areas for שבת are not the same as the rules for a גט. For a גט, the question is whether the husband would actually mind her using the spot.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume that 'separate area' means the same thing everywhere. On שבת, two roofs are separate. For a גט, a neighboring roof of the husband still counts because he would not mind.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a גט landing in the husband's property depends on what he is willing to lend her. It is not a technical boundary rule.

phrases.english: These words apply only regarding Shabbat,
but regarding a get –
it is because of being particular,
and people are not particular to this extent.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי מִילֵּי לְעִנְיַן שַׁבָּת, אֲבָל לְעִנְיַן גֵּט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits שמואל's rule from step 1 to שבת only.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A גט that lands on the husband's neighboring roof still divorces her, because a husband does not mind her using it.

steps.title: אביי's case of an inner courtyard inside an outer one
steps.stepSummary: אביי rules on a case with two courtyards. Hers is inside his, and his walls are taller. A גט thrown to her counts once it drops below the top of his outer walls.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: there are two courtyards, one inside the other. The inner one is hers and the outer one is his, and the outer walls are taller than the inner walls. He threw the גט to her. Once it reaches the space surrounded by the outer walls, she is divorced.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings a new case about when a thrown גט counts as having arrived in the wife's courtyard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a גט must be inside her courtyard. Here it is still above her own short walls, but it is already lower than his taller outer walls. אביי rules that this is already enough, even though it has not yet dropped below her walls.

phrases.english: Abaye said: two courtyards
this one inside that one,
the inner one is hers and the outer one is his,
and the walls of the outer one are taller than the inner ones;
and he threw it to her;
once it reached the airspace of the outer walls –
phrases.notes: He means it is above her courtyard and already lower than the top of his tall outer walls.

phrases.english: she is divorced.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: שְׁתֵּי חֲצֵרוֹת זוֹ לִפְנִים מִזּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: a גט thrown into an inner courtyard surrounded by taller outer walls.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the outer walls are taller, the גט counts as in her courtyard once it is below the height of the outer walls.

steps.title: Asking for the reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why אביי's ruling is true.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind אביי's ruling. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling is surprising. The גט has not yet passed below her own walls, so it is not clear why it already counts as hers.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind אביי's ruling in step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does the גט count as hers once it is below the outer walls, even though it is above her own walls?

steps.title: The outer walls protect the inner courtyard too
steps.stepSummary: The inner courtyard itself is guarded by the outer walls. So the space under the outer walls counts as part of her courtyard.
steps.simpleTranslation: The inner courtyard itself is protected by the walls of the outer courtyard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains אביי's ruling. The outer walls guard her courtyard as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A courtyard can acquire things for its owner because it is a guarded place. Here the taller outer walls are what really guard her courtyard. So once the גט is inside the space those walls protect, it counts as safely in her area.
steps.whatToRemember: A wife's courtyard acquires the גט because it is a guarded place. If taller outer walls guard her courtyard, the space inside those walls already counts as hers.

phrases.english: The inner courtyard itself –
is guarded by the walls of the outer one.

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּנִימִית גּוּפַהּ בִּמְחִיצוֹת הַחִיצוֹנָה קָא מִינַּטְרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The outer walls guard the inner courtyard, so the space within them counts as part of her guarded courtyard.

steps.title: Baskets work differently from courtyards
steps.stepSummary: With two baskets, one inside the other (inner is hers, outer is his), a גט that only reaches the air of her basket does not divorce her.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not so with baskets. Picture two baskets, one inside the other. The inner one is hers and the outer one is his. He threw the גט to her. Even if it reached the air of the inner basket, she is not divorced.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets the baskets case against אביי's courtyards case. With baskets, entering the airspace of her basket is not enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the courtyard case, her space began once the גט dropped below his outer walls, because those walls guard her courtyard. Baskets do not work that way. Reaching the air inside her basket does not yet count.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two cases. With courtyards, the air below his walls already counts as hers. With baskets, even the air inside her own basket does not count yet.

phrases.english: This is not so with regard to baskets
phrases.notes: He is contrasting this with אביי's case of two courtyards from just before.

phrases.english: two baskets, this one inside that one
the inner is hers and the outer is his
and he threw it to her
even if it reached the airspace of the inner basket
she is not divorced

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts the courtyard case of אביי with a case of nested baskets.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With nested baskets, a גט that reaches the air of her inner basket does not divorce her.

steps.title: Why is the basket case different?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason the airspace of her basket does not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the גט in the baskets case does not work. This sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With courtyards, the airspace counted. So we need to know what makes baskets different.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the baskets ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why reaching the air of her basket does not divorce her.

steps.title: The גט has not landed yet
steps.stepSummary: The reason is that the גט has not come to rest inside the basket.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it has not yet come to rest.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a basket only acquires what actually lands in it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A courtyard is a place, and its guarded air counts as part of it. A basket is a vessel, and it acquires only once the item rests inside. So the גט must actually land in her basket.

phrases.english: Because it did not rest

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A basket acquires only once the גט actually rests inside it, not while it is in its air.

steps.title: Even landing should not help
steps.stepSummary: Even if the גט lands, her basket sits inside his basket. That is like a buyer's vessel sitting in the seller's property.
steps.simpleTranslation: And when it does rest, what difference does that make? It is like a buyer's vessel in the seller's domain!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that landing would work. Her basket sits inside his basket, so it is in his domain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A buyer's vessel that sits in the seller's property does not acquire for the buyer. Here her basket is inside his basket, so it should not acquire the גט for her either. That makes the line "it did not rest" seem pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: And when it rests, what of it?

phrases.english: And when it rests, what of it?

phrases.aramaic: כִּלְיוֹ שֶׁל לוֹקֵחַ בִּרְשׁוּת מוֹכֵר הוּא!
phrases.english: It is the vessel of a buyer in the domain of the seller!
phrases.notes: Her basket is like the buyer's vessel, and his basket around it is like the seller's property.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the גט works once it rests in her basket.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Her basket sits inside his basket, and a buyer's vessel in the seller's domain does not acquire.

steps.title: The outer basket has no bottom
steps.stepSummary: The case is one where the outer basket has no bottom. Her basket really rests on the ground, not inside his vessel.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are we dealing with here? A basket that has no bottom.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by narrowing the case. His outer basket is bottomless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If his basket has no bottom, her basket is not sitting inside his vessel. It sits on the ground. So once the גט lands in her basket, she is divorced.

keyTerms.meaning: With what are we dealing here?

steps.whatToRemember: With baskets, the גט must actually land in her basket. This works only because his outer basket is bottomless, so her basket is not inside his property.

phrases.english: With what are we dealing here?
With a basket that has no bottom
phrases.notes: He means his outer basket, so her inner basket is really resting on the ground.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9 by limiting the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Her basket sits inside his basket, so it is in his domain and cannot acquire.
steps.terutzMaskana: The outer basket has no bottom, so her basket rests on the ground and acquires once the גט lands.

steps.title: The משנה: Divorcing with an old גט
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי allow divorcing with a גט ישן and בית הלל forbid it. A גט ישן is one where the husband was alone with his wife after writing it.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי say: a man may divorce his wife with an old גט. בית הלל forbid it. What is an old גט? Any case where he was alone with her after he wrote it for her.
steps.whatsHappening: A brand new משנה begins, starting a fresh topic. It records a dispute between בית שמאי and בית הלל and defines the term גט ישן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A husband wrote a גט for his wife but did not hand it over right away. In the meantime he was alone with her. The question is whether that גט can still be used. בית שמאי say yes and בית הלל say no.

keyTerms.meaning: An 'old' גט: one written before the husband was alone with his wife

steps.confusionAlert: Old does not mean the גט is old in years. It means the husband was alone with his wife after it was written, even if that happened soon after.

phrases.english: MISHNA
Beit Shammai say:
A man may divorce his wife with an old bill of divorce.
And Beit Hillel forbid it.
And what is an old bill of divorce?
Any case where he was alone with her
after he wrote it for her.
phrases.notes: He means alone with her after writing the גט but before giving it to her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic, unrelated to the baskets discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי permit divorcing with a גט ישן and בית הלל forbid it. A גט ישן is one where the husband was alone with his wife after writing it.

steps.title: What is the root of their dispute?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what principle בית שמאי and בית הלל disagree about.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking for the reason behind the disagreement in the משנה. This sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gave the two rulings but no reasons. The גמרא wants to know what underlying idea each side holds.

phrases.english: GEMARA
About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the dispute in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The principle underlying the dispute between בית שמאי and בית הלל about a גט ישן.

steps.title: The dispute is about a protective decree
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל make a גזרה out of concern that people will say her divorce came before her son. בית שמאי do not make this גזרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי hold that we do not make a decree out of concern that people will say her גט came before her son. בית הלל hold that we do make a decree out of concern that people will say her גט came before her son.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: the two sides disagree about whether to make a protective rule, a גזרה, against using an old גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The date written on the גט is earlier than the day she actually receives it. If she has a child from her husband in between, people might look at the date and think the child was conceived after she was divorced. בית הלל forbid the old גט to prevent that rumor, and בית שמאי are not worried about it.

keyTerms.meaning: A protective rule made by the חכמים
Her גט came before her son

steps.whyThisMatters: The halacha follows בית הלל, so an old גט should not be used in the first place. The next step limits how far this גזרה reaches.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai hold:
we do not say there is a decree
lest people say
her bill of divorce came before her son.
phrases.notes: People would see the early date on the גט and think the child was conceived after the divorce.

phrases.english: And Beit Hillel hold:
we do say there is a decree
lest people say
her bill of divorce came before her son.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי סָבְרִי לָא אָמְרִינַן גְּזֵרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They disagree whether to make a גזרה out of concern that people will think her divorce came before her child was conceived. בית הלל make this גזרה and בית שמאי do not.

steps.title: If she already remarried, she stays married
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא in the name of שמואל: if a woman remarried using a גט ישן, she does not have to leave her new husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said in the name of שמואל: if she got married, she does not have to leave.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא adds a ruling: even according to בית הלל, if the woman already remarried with an old גט, the marriage stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל's rule is only a protective גזרה. It tells us not to use an old גט in the first place. It is not strong enough to break up a second marriage that already happened. So the גט really works, and the concern only applies at the start.

keyTerms.meaning: She got married, here meaning to a second husband
She does not have to leave her new husband

steps.whatToRemember: A גט ישן should not be used because of בית הלל's גזרה that people may think her divorce came before her son. But if she already remarried with it, שמואל rules she stays married.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think בית הלל hold the old גט is no good at all. It is forbidden in the first place only because of a גזרה, which is why a second marriage after the fact can stand.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said that Shmuel said:
If she got married, she does not have to leave.
phrases.notes: He means she remarried using the old גט, and she may stay with her second husband.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits בית הלל's גזרה from step 13. It applies at the start, not after she has already remarried.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If a woman remarried using a גט ישן, she does not have to leave her second husband.

steps.title: A second version: she may remarry even from the start
steps.stepSummary: Some say רבי אבא quoted שמואל more leniently: a woman divorced with a גט ישן may remarry even from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: Others say that רבי אבא said in the name of שמואל: if she was divorced with an old גט, she may marry even from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second report of רבי אבא's quote from שמואל. In this report, the ruling is even more lenient than the one in Step 14.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 14, the ruling was only after the fact: if she already remarried, she does not have to leave. Here, the ruling goes further. A woman divorced with a גט ישן may remarry right away, with no need for a new גט.

keyTerms.meaning: There are those who say. This introduces a second version of a teaching.
From the start, before anything was done. Not just after the fact.

steps.whatToRemember: There are two versions of שמואל's view on a גט ישן. In the first, after the fact she does not leave her new husband. In the second, she may remarry with it even from the start.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two versions. Step 14 only protects a marriage that already happened. This step allows the marriage to begin in the first place.

phrases.english: And there are those who say:
Rabbi Abba said that Shmuel said:
If she was divorced,
phrases.notes: He means divorced with a גט ישן, the old גט from Step 14.

phrases.english: she may marry even from the start.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי, אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, more lenient version of the same statement quoted in Step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman divorced with a גט ישן may remarry with it even from the start.

steps.title: New משנה: a גט dated in an improper way
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists ways of dating a גט improperly: by an improper kingdom, by Media or Greece, or by the building or destruction of the בית המקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If he dated the גט by a kingdom that is not proper, by the kingdom of Media, by the kingdom of Greece, from the building of the בית המקדש, or from the destruction of the בית המקדש…
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a list of wrong ways to write the date in a גט. This step sets up the cases, and the ruling comes in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גט must be dated the official way, which in the time of the משנה meant counting the years of the ruling kingdom. Each case here uses a different, unofficial way of counting years. The משנה will soon rule that such a גט does not work properly.

keyTerms.meaning: In the name of a kingdom, meaning dating the document by that kingdom's years.
Not proper or not fitting, a kingdom not used for official dating.
The destruction of the בית המקדש.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
If he wrote it by a kingdom that is not proper;
phrases.notes: He means he wrote the date in the גט by counting that kingdom's years.

phrases.english: by the kingdom of Media;
by the kingdom of Greece;
counting from the building of the Temple; counting from the destruction of the Temple;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic: improper dating in a גט.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A list of improper ways to date a גט. The ruling for these cases comes in Steps 17-23.

steps.title: Wrong place written, and she must leave both husbands
steps.stepSummary: Writing the wrong location (east and west switched) is another faulty case. In all these cases, if she remarried, she must leave both men and needs a גט from both.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he was in the east and wrote 'in the west,' or in the west and wrote 'in the east,' she must leave this man and that man, and she needs a גט from this one and from that one.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a case where the גט names the wrong place. Then it gives the ruling for all the cases: if she remarried with such a גט, she must leave both husbands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the גט was not written properly, the חכמים do not let it count as a proper divorce, so her second marriage cannot stand. She is also not allowed to go back to the first husband, so she must leave him too. Each man must give her a proper גט.

keyTerms.meaning: She must leave, meaning the marriage must end.
From this one and from that one, meaning both husbands.

steps.confusionAlert: The ruling 'she must leave both' is not only for the east-west case. It applies to every case in the list, including the dating mistakes from Step 16.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a technical mistake in a גט can have very heavy results: both marriages are ended.

phrases.english: He was in the east and wrote 'in the west' as the place in the גט;
in the west and wrote 'in the east' —
she must leave this one and that one,
phrases.notes: She remarried using this faulty גט, so 'this one and that one' are her first and second husbands.

phrases.english: and she needs a get from this one and from that one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another faulty case and gives the ruling for all the cases in the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If she remarried with an improperly dated or placed גט, she must leave both husbands and receive a גט from each.

steps.title: She loses her money rights from both husbands
steps.stepSummary: In these cases she gets no כתובה, no produce, no food, and no worn clothing from either husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: And she has no כתובה, no produce, no food, and no worn clothing, not from this husband and not from that husband.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes the ruling by listing the money rights the woman loses. She can claim none of them from either husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a wife has several money rights from her husband. Here the משנה takes all of them away, from both the first and the second husband. So beyond ending both marriages, she also loses her money rights.

keyTerms.meaning: The marriage contract payment a wife receives when the marriage ends.
Produce, the profits from her property that her husband used.
Worn-out items, like her clothing that her husband used.

steps.whatToRemember: With an improperly dated or placed גט, if she remarried: she leaves both husbands, needs a גט from both, and loses her כתובה and other money rights from both.

phrases.english: And she has no ketubah
and no produce and no food
and no worn clothing —
phrases.notes: These are worn-out items that belonged to her and that her husband used.

phrases.aramaic: לֹא עַל זֶה, וְלֹא עַל זֶה.
phrases.english: not from this one, and not from that one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the משנה's ruling by adding the money rights she loses.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: She loses her כתובה, produce, food, and worn clothing rights from both husbands.

steps.title: She must return whatever she took
steps.stepSummary: If the woman already took any of the payments from either husband, she must give them back.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she took any of these from either husband, she must return it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds to the list from step 18. She may not keep any כתובה money, produce, food, or clothing she already received from either husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 18 said she cannot collect these things. This step goes further: even if she already collected them, she has to give them back. The penalty covers money she has in hand, not only money she is still owed.

keyTerms.meaning: from this one or from that one (either husband)

phrases.english: If she took from this one or from that one
phrases.notes: 'This one' and 'that one' are her two husbands. What she took means the things listed in step 18.

phrases.english: she must return it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends step 18 from money she cannot collect to money she must give back.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Anything she received from either husband must be returned.

steps.title: A child from either husband is a ממזר
steps.stepSummary: A child born from either husband in this situation has the status of a ממזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the child is a ממזר, whether from this husband or from that one.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה rules on the status of children. A child she has from either husband is a ממזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her גט from the first husband was faulty, so her second marriage is treated as a forbidden relationship. The משנה gives ממזר status to a child from either man, not only the second. This means a child conceived after she married the second husband, not children born during her first marriage before the גט.

keyTerms.meaning: a child born from a forbidden relationship, who may not marry into the general community

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume only the second husband's child is affected. The משנה says the child is a ממזר "from this one or from that one," so it applies to either husband.

phrases.english: And the child is a ממזר from this one or from that one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from money penalties to the status of children.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A child born from either husband is a ממזר.

steps.title: Neither husband may become impure for her burial
steps.stepSummary: If the husbands are כהנים, neither one may become ritually impure to bury her.
steps.simpleTranslation: Neither this husband nor that husband may become impure for her.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה says neither husband is treated as her real husband for burial. Normally a כהן may become impure to bury his wife, but here neither husband may.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן may only become impure for close relatives, and a wife is one of them. Since neither marriage counts as a proper one here, neither husband gets this permission.

keyTerms.meaning: become ritually impure (here, for a burial)
this one and that one (both husbands)

phrases.english: And neither this one nor that one becomes impure for her,
phrases.notes: This is about husbands who are כהנים and whether they may come in contact with her body when she dies.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a ritual penalty to the earlier money and status penalties.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן husband from either marriage may not become impure for her.

steps.title: Neither husband gets a husband's usual rights
steps.stepSummary: Neither husband is entitled to her found objects, her earnings, or the power to cancel her vows.
steps.simpleTranslation: Neither this husband nor that husband has rights to what she finds, to what she earns, or to cancel her vows.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists three rights a husband normally has over his wife, and says neither husband has any of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These rights come with a valid marriage. She loses her rights as a wife (step 18), and in the same way both men lose their rights as husbands.
steps.whatToRemember: The penalty works in both directions. She loses a wife's rights, and both men lose a husband's rights.

phrases.english: And neither this one nor that one is entitled –
not to what she finds,
and not to her earnings,
and not to cancelling her vows.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from what she loses to what the husbands lose.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Neither husband has rights to her found objects, her earnings, or her vows.

steps.title: A בת ישראל becomes disqualified from marrying a כהן
steps.stepSummary: If she was a בת ישראל, she is now disqualified from marrying into כהונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she was a בת ישראל, she becomes disqualified from the כהונה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds one more penalty about her future. A בת ישראל in this situation may no longer marry a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her second marriage was really a forbidden relationship, because the faulty גט did not fully free her. A woman with that kind of relationship is forbidden to a כהן, so she loses the right to marry one.

keyTerms.meaning: a Jewish woman who is not from a family of כהנים or לוים

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the faulty גט affects her for the rest of her life, even beyond these two marriages.

phrases.english: If she was a בת ישראל –
she becomes disqualified from the priesthood.
phrases.notes: He means she may no longer marry a כהן.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיְתָה בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל – נִפְסֶלֶת מִן הַכְּהוּנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a penalty about her future marriage options, beyond the two current husbands.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בת ישראל in this case becomes forbidden to marry a כהן.
